subject: design
intro: Design leads into the product and communication professions: shaping manufactured goods, graphics and interfaces, tuning them to human bodies, and drawing the technical documents that get them made.

roles.title: Commercial and Industrial Designers
roles.what: Design and develop manufactured products such as cars, home appliances and children's toys, combining artistic talent with research on product use, marketing and materials to create the most functional and appealing product design.
roles.where: The course is this role end to end: influences on designing (user needs, anthropometrics, aesthetics, sustainability), designing principles, communicating designs, making principles and the full material classification.

roles.title: Graphic Designers
roles.what: Design or create graphics to meet specific commercial or promotional needs, such as packaging, displays or logos, using a variety of media to achieve artistic or decorative effects.
roles.where: The graphic products option — technical drawing methods, presentation, methods of communicating information — plus CAD from the common content, is the daily toolkit for briefs like packaging and identity.

roles.title: Web and Digital Interface Designers
roles.what: Design digital user interfaces or websites, developing and testing layouts, functionality and navigation for compatibility and usability across browsers and devices, and evaluating designs against accessibility standards.
roles.where: Communicating designs covers the drawing and modelling techniques that become wireframing; the technology unit's designing with AI, and unit 1's user needs and inclusivity topics, map onto interface and accessibility work.

roles.title: Human Factors Engineers and Ergonomists
roles.what: Design objects, facilities and environments to optimise human well-being and overall system performance, applying theory, principles and data about how humans behave and perform when using technology.
roles.where: Unit 1.1 is the ergonomic core: anthropometrics and ergonomics, user needs, safety and inclusivity; the structures and mechanisms units supply the physical systems thinking the role applies to products and workplaces.

roles.title: Architectural and Civil Drafters
roles.what: Prepare detailed drawings of architectural and structural features of buildings, and topographical relief maps for civil engineering projects such as highways, bridges and public works, using knowledge of building materials and mathematics.
roles.where: Drawing techniques — freehand, orthographic, isometric, exploded and CAD — plus the material classification and structures units' loads, forces and reinforcement, are exactly what architectural and civil drafting renders precisely.
